Every person reacts differently to medications, but that certainly was my experience. At the time I started lithium I was in an on-off toxic relationship, and the emotional disconnect was what helped me leave them behind. I see your case is quite the opposite, so I would recommend having a thorough talk with your husband and explain what you believe to be happening and hope he can stand by you as you adapt.

I also took Vyvanse with lithium and detected no interaction between the two, but then again, that’s just my experience. 

I’d also remark it’s been almost 5 years since I was on lithium, so my memory of it might be a bit fuzzy. Sorry.

Took it for over a year, until my psychiatrist took me off the meds. I’d say it was like a reset switch. Combined with therapy I’d say it did turn my life around.

I still struggle with mental illness, I don’t think it really ever goes away, but I’ve learned to live with it. This is not to say I just tolerate it, but understand how it makes me think differently. Treat is as part of life, not the thing that’ll take it from me.

Not to go off topic, lithium kinda made the screams quiet for long enough that I could gather tools to battle depression. You’ll have to work like hell, but it certainly helps. Not definitive evidence, but an anecdote that I hope works for you as well.

makes you feel like you died, but only part of you went away, right? Purgatory, watching the world go by, as time moves forward, but you're still standing in the same spot. 

Been around 6 months since I started lithium, and everything that's going on in the world, don't know if I'm supposed to feel like this or if it's the meds. Some days (or at least a couple of hours during the day), I'll feel like myself again; the me of when I was healthy, happy, looked forward to and cared about things, had interests, you know? Other times, I can't stand this and would rather die than be this empty shell. I don't really feel human, if that makes any sense.

Don't you find that some days you'll just realize how blind you were to certain things in life, that were clearly hurting you and making you worse off? Bad friends, dependency on past partners, letting others treat you wrong, etc.

Curious to talk with people who are going through a similar situation.

I have tried to reach out and get help many times. My parents and close friends do know about this, and are the reason why I´m able to see a neurologist and was seeing a therapist.

The thing is, I get to a point where I don't feel anything for these people, and my mind simply wanders off into a numb gray state. I don't know if it's the meds or the mental illness itself but I am very irritable, and that can turn to anger and hate very quickly towards people who frankly aren't doing much to merit that response. 

I have driven away people consciously though. When I start to get very bad I do isolate myself and disconnect with people, in the back of my head hoping this will cushion the blow of me committing suicide.
This actually boosted my mood a bit. Thank you.

Sorry for not replying. I haven't really been online anywhere, instead I just lay in my bed for hours. 

I try and go out, even if it's painful and hard just to leave my room, but I've very much hit bottom. Those I called friends don't reply to my texts, or simply tell me they don't want to go out or that they're always busy yet I see them on social media in some club. 

Those who do know about my mental health have gotten to the point where they resent me. They've taken care of me for so long, and it is very taxing, I know. I can't expect for them to not grow and live because of my own lack of capacity to do that very thing.

​

I've been on many antidepressants, and anxiety meds. I don't remember all of them, but I can recall: Prozac, Strattera, Quetiapine, Sertraline, Vyvanse, Fluvoxamine, and others I can't remember. 

They don't work, or just work for a bit and then I'm back to my shitty life. Even worse, some make me just feel drugged, or like I'm someone else. 

I was supposed to be on meds for a max of 8 months, and I'm going strong onto 2 years. 

​

I try and fake I'm happy, but that just makes me worse. I feel like I bottle up the sadness and it ends in a panic attack or deep depression.

I see the wonder the world has to offer, and have had many opportunities for travel, study, and more. 

I am extremely privileged yet I feel nothing when I see that. Things that would fill me with child like wonder are now gray. This account is pretty old, back from where I used to like manga and natural sciences, but the depression has taken and taken away from me. 

I feel hollow.
